title: Webel
summary: A home-services marketplace in production, with millions of users. I'm the web lead: Organizations, marketplace, programmatic SEO and the internal dashboard.
problem: Webel is the Amazon of home services. What it needs to solve is friction and discovery: small professionals (home cleaners, English tutors, handymen, caregivers) and people who need to hire those services without always relying on word of mouth.
audience: People who need a service, professionals offering their work, and companies managing services for their teams.
role: Frontend tech lead: React and TypeScript across several critical products, growing the web team and bringing AI into the development workflow.
responsibilities: Webel Organizations, the B2B platform: employees, services, calendar, leads, chat, tax details, service areas, schedules and payouts.
Marketplace core: search and browsing the offer. Full migration from Angular to React; today it's a storefront that redirects to the apps, with no login or users.
Programmatic SEO from scratch in Astro: over 50k templates, structured data and performance. Top organic result on Google for «Limpieza a domicilio en Madrid».
The internal dashboard the team runs operations with.
Architecture unification across Organizations, dashboard and marketplace, and extracting the design system into a shared component library.
Migrating 100+ custom emails to React Email, with better rendering and bugs near zero.
Automating the development flow with skills, agents and design-system docs built for agents (Cursor, Codex, Claude, OpenCode).
decisions: Unify the stack on React across the big products, including the Angular to React marketplace migration, so the team works in one language.
Extract the design system into a shared component library across products.
Build programmatic SEO from scratch in Astro.
Bring AI into day-to-day work: architecture, network-layer and gitflow skills, plus DS docs you can drop into any project.
outcomes: Web went from one of the worst teams for tech debt and outdated stack to pretty much the fastest-moving one.
Modern stack: React in the apps, React Email for mail, Astro for SEO.
Bugs near zero and solid interfaces, with a responsive layer that holds up.
Performance, observability and product proposals that made it into the team's work.
